text: The October food result was provisional because a row was rejected. I want to automate finance imports and cannot let a partial report look complete. Add an opt-in --strict mode: if any row would be skipped, emit the warnings but no report on stdout and exit 2. Good data should still produce the report. First give me a short human-facing progress update after inspecting the current behavior, then continue implementing and testing this. Update the handoff with the safe import command.

One important workflow detail while you work: I rerun this into an existing CSV used by finance. A failed strict run must leave that existing file intact. Add a small safe export command or script that writes a temporary file and replaces the target only on success, and prove this with an existing output file. Keep the existing non-strict CLI behavior unchanged.

One final operational question: if run_report.sh exits 2 but the old CSV is still present, should my importer read that old file? Give me the exact exit-code policy and the command to use, briefly. I want the automation to avoid importing stale data as well as partial data.

Please remove the confusing pipeline example. Give only a tested if/then pattern that runs the import step on exit 0 and skips it on every failure. Preserve the original nonzero exit status in the failure branch so cron reports the failure. Demonstrate the failure path locally with a harmless marker standing in for the importer; do not contact any external service.
